messages:
maria_oss: Quick question — during today's canary I noticed some traffic meant for variant-B kept landing on baseline when `X-Canary` header was present. Anyone else see this?
ajay: I saw a few traces too. At first glance it looked like header-matching should win over weighted split, but our docs are fuzzy.
tayler: Our routing docs say header rules have precedence, then path, then weights. But the runtime has this helper that normalizes headers to lowercase before matching. Could that be it?
maria_oss: We sent `X-Canary: B` (capital X). If the router lowercases to `x-canary` but the rule expects `X-Canary` literal, would that mismatch?
jun: The rule matcher uses canonicalized header keys, but the canary check does an exact value match on the header value. Do we have any logging showing the header value the router saw?
observability-bot: New log stream: canary-routing/maria-1934567890 — sample of 10 requests attached.
ajay: Sample shows header value as "b" (lowercase) for a bunch of requests, while the canary rules expect "B". That explains why they fell through to weighted baseline.
tayler: Hmm. Where are we normalizing values to lowercase? The agent that extracts headers for the telemetry pipeline lowercases values for indexing. Not the router itself. Looks like the ingest pipeline mutated it before the match.
maria_oss: So two failures: 1) pipeline should not mutate headers before routing, 2) our rule semantics need to be explicit about case-sensitivity.
jun: Agreed. Short-term: add a fallback route that checks both casings. Example patch:```yaml
- match:
    headers:
      X-Canary: "B"
  destination: variant-B
- match:
    headers:
      x-canary: "b"
  destination: variant-B
```
ajay: That hack would work but ugly. Better to make router normalize both keys and values consistently. We should also add a telemetry guardrail that counts header-normalization mismatches.
tayler: UX note: console rollout UI should warn when header-match canaries are case-sensitive. Users assume headers are case-insensitive (key) and sometimes case-preserving for values. We need copy.
maria_oss: For the immediate canary ramp-down: can we add a weighted override to force 100% to variant-B for the affected cohort (trace IDs from logs)?
jun: Yes, we can create a short-lived split rule keyed on trace-id prefix:```json
{"match":{"trace_id_prefix":"cb97"},"weight":{"variant-B":100}}
```
ajay: Deploy-bot, can you schedule that change now with a 10m TTL?
deploy-bot: Received request. Creating rollout change: canary-for-cb97 -> applying 100% to variant-B. Will auto-revert after 10m.
observability-bot: Telemetry alert created: HeaderMismatchRate > 0.5% for canary-headers. Rule attached to eng-platform.
maria_oss: Thanks. Follow-ups: (1) fix pipeline so routing sees raw headers, (2) add normalization tests, (3) update console UI copy + tooltip, (4) add regression test in CI to simulate mixed-case values. I'll file a short RFC.
tayler: I'll take the RFC for the UI text. Ajay/Jun, can you take the runtime + pipeline fixes?
ajay: On it. I'll prototype a small change to ensure router uses raw request headers and does a normalize-to-lowercase-for-keys-only policy, and expose a config flag for value-case-sensitivity.
jun: I'll update the ingestion lambda to stop mutating header values. Also adding a unit test that runs the canary matcher against samples.
maria_oss: Cool. Post the RFC link here when you have it and ping eng-ml if this affects any inference headers. :thumbsup:
ajay: RFC: https://go/internal/rfcs/1934567890-canary-header-normalization — draft uploaded.
maria_oss: Great, closing this thread once the TTL reverts and telemetry looks green. Thanks all!
